title: Hobby Watch: This Week’s Biggest Trading Card Stories
body_markdown:
Here at Courtyard, we’re just as passionate about trading cards as you are. Some of us are chasing 1-of-1s, while others are still riding the high of a Pikachu pull. No matter what’s in your binder—or your digital vault—we all have one thing in common: an appetite for Hobby news that never quits. So, without further ado, here’s what came across our feeds throughout the week.


Whether you’re humming[the Space Jam theme song](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J9FImc2LOr8) every time a vintage Michael Jordan card sets a new all-time high, or you couldn’t believe your eyes when you saw the price paid for a League of Legends card, this week had a little something for every part of The Hobby.


## **Football’s Chasing a New Kind of Debut:**


As Topps continues to consolidate licenses across the MLB, NBA, and NFL, the latter is the latest to see one of the brand’s crowning achievements: Debut Patches. Starting with the 2026 rookie class, every NFL rookie will wear a Debut Patch on their jersey for their first game. No more cloth that’s “not from any specific game or event.” Now, you know exactly when that patch of jersey was worn. In fact, you might’ve watched it live!


These genuinely unrepeatable pieces of history are a great turnaround for the Hobby. Over in The Association, NBA fans have fawned over[Cooper Flagg](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Cooper%20Flagg&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ’s[1/1 Rookie Debut Patch Autograph](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/hobby-watch-this-weeks-biggest-trading-card-stories) , which was won in a $515 break by a lucky collector who now stands to make millions off of the Mavericks star.


Back on the gridiron, NFL fans don’t have to wait for Week 1 to get their football fix: Last week’s release of Topps Flagship Football has already been a hit, with the 1/1[Caleb Williams](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Caleb%20Williams&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) “All Kings” card[pulled live on a break](https://www.tiktok.com/@sportscardinv/video/7678442450679074078) shortly after its release.


Whether you’re chasing quarterbacks like[Josh Allen](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=josh%20allen&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) and[Patrick Mahomes](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Patrick%20Mahomes&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , or you’ve got your eyes on enigmatic wide receivers like[CeeDee Lamb](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Ceedee%20Lamb&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) or[Marvin Harrison Jr.](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Marvin%20Harrison%20Jr.&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , our[Football Packs](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=football) are loaded with stars to start your season off right.


## **A New Gem Hits the Diamond:**


It’s your turn, baseball collectors. 2026 Topps Chrome Sapphire Baseball was released this week, and it’s a big one.


The Hidden Gems insert is headlined by[Bobby Witt Jr.](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Bobby%20Witt%20Jr&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ,[Shohei Ohtani](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Shohei%20Ohtani&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , Samuel Basallo, Nick Kurtz, and Jac Caglianone, while the Sapphire Selections autograph checklist leans on superstar Ohtani again, alongside fellow former MVPs[Aaron Judge](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Aaron%20Judge&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) and[Mike Trout](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Mike%20Trout&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) . The true grail, though, is the Padparadscha parallel, a 1/1 chase named after one of the rarest sapphires on Earth.


Those chasing rookies should keep an eye on rookie studs like[Munetaka Murakami](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Munetaka%20Murakami&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ,[Kevin McGonigle](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Kevin%20McGonigle&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , and[JJ Wetherholt](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=JJ%20Wetherholt&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , all of whom can be found on our[Marketplace](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BrefinementList%5D%5Bmetadata.Category%5D%5B0%5D=Baseball) , while our[Baseball Packs](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=baseball) have all five tools you need to build the perfect collection to dominate the diamond.


## **Gotta Snap ‘Em All:**


Pokémon keeps finding new ways to celebrate its 30th birthday. This week,[The Pokémon Company teamed up with Polaroid](https://www.polaroid.com/en_us/discover/polaroid-pokemon-collaboration) for a collection of special-edition instant cameras: a Polaroid Go Generation 3 in Pikachu and Sylveon designs, and a Poké Ball Polaroid Now, complete with themed film featuring 18 different designs, a Poké Ball camera strap, and a circular photo album that might top the cards themselves. Pre-orders are open through September 28, but we have a feeling these collectible items will be hard to get.


The TCG company’s latest collaboration is just one of many leading up to the 30th anniversary, with the special 30th Anniversary Celebration set officially releasing on September 16. Mark your calendars, because if last week’s news about the $1.3 million Illustrator Pikachu sale is any indication, these cards won’t stick around long.


Craving your own nostalgia hit? Not only do we have[Pokémon Packs](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=pkmn) ready to rip, but we’ve also got a limited-time drop of our own: the[Pokémon Ghost](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/pkmn-ghost-pack) ,[Pokémon Reaper](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/pkmn-reaper-pack) , and[Pokémon Inferno](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine/pkmn-inferno-pack) , each with increasingly hot value ceilings ranging from 16x to 32x, and all the way up to 64x. Get ‘em while they’re sizzling!


## **The Big Three, Bigger Than Ever:**


Vintage never really goes out of style, but this week throwback hoops went on a serious run.[Cajun Cardboard](https://www.youtube.com/@CajunCardboard) —one of The Hobby’s most trusted sources for all things ‘90s basketball cards—offered a great breakdown of just how much money is currently pouring into vintage[Michael Jordan](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Michael%20Jordan&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ,[Kobe Bryant](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Kobe%20Bryant&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , and[LeBron James](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=LeBron%20James&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) cardboard, and the numbers are staggering.


Similarly[a 2022 Shaquille O’Neal card](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Shaquille%20O%27Neal&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) that sold for $21,600 just nine months ago was recently sold for $45,600. While the card itself isn’t vintage, Shaq retired 15 years ago, showcasing the staying power of players from bygone eras. Shaq has been undervalued for a while, but his Card Ladder index shows that the Big Aristotle is up 93.54% since June. As demand for older cards continues to grow, there might be opportunities around players from years past like[Allen Iverson](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Allen%20Iverson&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ,[Tracy McGrady](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Tracy%20McGrady&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , and more.


Whether you’re a lifelong Bulls fan or you’re just catching vintage fever, our[Basketball Packs](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=basketball) are loaded with history and nostalgia.


## **The Rift Just Delivered a Record:**


Not every trading card’s story starts on a field or a court. Riftbound, the physical card game built around Riot Games’ hit Multiplayer Online Battle Arena (MOBA) League of Legends, just posted the biggest sale in its short history. On August 12, Hong Kong retailer HKTCG paid roughly $130,000 for[the 1/1 National Champion Ezreal card](https://bo3.gg/games/news/riftbound-ezreal-card-sells-for-130000-setting-new-record) , topping the game’s previous record of roughly $115,000.


Launched last year, Riftbound’s recent sales are sending a serious signal throughout the TCG space. Simply put, this isn’t a simple esports tie-in, this is a legit TCG that aims to follow in the footsteps of storied brands like[Magic: The Gathering](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=magic_the_gathering) , which has become pricier in its own right.


## **Hobby Highlights:**


From baseball rookies to vintage basketball and three decades of Pokémon, this week proved that The Hobby is bigger than any one sport or set.


Want to get in on the action? Head to our[Marketplace](https://courtyard.io/marketplace) or grab[a pack](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine) and see where trading cards will take you.
